## What's new in 1.8.3

The Gundil icon shows in the Linux taskbar and dock.

- **Linux (AppImage and tar.gz):** the taskbar or dock used to show a generic icon. Docks such as GNOME's (Ubuntu) and KDE's on Wayland take an app's icon from its entry in the app menu, which an AppImage doesn't have because it isn't installed. Now the app adds that entry itself the first time it starts: **Gundil Intercom** appears in your app menu with its icon, the taskbar shows the right icon, and you can pin it to the dock. The entry points to the AppImage where it is now. If you move the AppImage, start it once from its new place to update the entry, and if you delete it, the entry disappears from the menu. If the icon is still generic the very first time, close the app (tray → Exit) and start it again.
  - It writes `~/.local/share/applications/com.p2pintercom.p2p_intercom.desktop` and `~/.local/share/icons/hicolor/*/apps/gundil-intercom.png`. To undo, delete them. To skip it, start the app with `GUNDIL_NO_DESKTOP_ENTRY=1`.
  - With **AppImageLauncher** (or Gear Lever, appimaged), which add their own menu entry when they integrate the AppImage, the app doesn't add a second one, so the menu lists Gundil Intercom only once. If an earlier 1.8.3 download already showed *Gundil Intercom* and *Gundil Intercom (1)*, replace it with this one and start it once: the extra entry is removed.
  - The window also has the icon in every size from 16 to 128 pixels (X11 taskbars, Alt+Tab), instead of only one.
  - The "Start automatically" entry (Settings) now has the icon too. Turn it off and on again to update an existing one.
- **Other platforms:** Windows (program, installer, taskbar, tray), Mac, iPhone and Android already use the same Gundil icon; nothing changes there.

Upgrading: install over 1.8.2 or 1.8.1, and your cameras, peers and settings are kept. If your Android phone still has a version before 1.8.1, see the 1.8.1 notes: uninstall it first (export the list before, import it after). Works with 1.2.0 – 1.8.2 intercoms.
